030package dev.visdb.seesaw.formatting;
031
032import java.text.ParseException;
033import java.util.Objects;
034import java.util.function.BiFunction;
035
036import javax.swing.JFormattedTextField;
037import javax.swing.JFormattedTextField.AbstractFormatter;
038import javax.swing.text.DefaultFormatter;
039import javax.swing.text.DefaultFormatterFactory;
040
041/**
042 * Base for SS formatter factories; supports allow null and ssFormat.
043 */
044@SuppressWarnings("serial")
045public abstract class FormatterFactory extends DefaultFormatterFactory {
046  private final SsFormat ssFormat;
047  private final AbstractFormatter converter;
048  private final BiFunction<JFormattedTextField, AbstractFormatter, Boolean> containsUserText;
049
050  /**
051   * To build a new FormatterFactory with the specified parameters. Unless noted,
052   * a parameter is used when constructing the MaskFormatter.<p>
053   * <p>
054   * @see <em>Effective Java</em> Item 2 about override.
055   * @param <T>
056   */
057  abstract protected static class Builder<T extends Builder<T>> {
058    private AbstractFormatter converter = null;
059    private SsFormat ssFormat = null;
060    private BiFunction<JFormattedTextField, AbstractFormatter, Boolean> containsUserText;
061
062    /**
063     * May be used by a formatter to assist string2Value and value2String.
064     * For example, the Ss mask formatters work with strings, the converter
065     * converts string to value; like a Date.
066     * It's the last step in stringToValue; it produces the Value
067     * in the formatted text field.
068     * @param val
069     * @return  builder
070     */
071    public T converter(AbstractFormatter val) {
072      converter = val;
073      return self();
074    }
075    /**
076     * *  The {@link SsFormat} used when generating this format factory.
077     * @param val
078     * @return  builder
079     */
080    public T ssFormat(SsFormat val) {
081      ssFormat = val;
082      return self();
083    }
084    /**
085     *  This overrides the default check for user input data present. The default
086     * check is done using {@link FormatterAssist#userText(java.lang.String,
087     * java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.Character)}. If set, this
088     * is used by {@link SsFormattedTextField#containsUserText() }.
089     * @param val
090     * @return  builder
091     */
092    public T containsUserText(BiFunction<JFormattedTextField, AbstractFormatter, Boolean> val) {
093      containsUserText = val;
094      return self();
095    }
096
097    /**
098     *
099     * @return
100     */
101    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
102    protected T self() {
103      return (T) this;
104    }
105
106    /**
107     * builder
108     * @return converter
109     */
110    public AbstractFormatter getConverter() {
111      return converter;
112    }
113  }
114
115  /**
116   * The Format used to create factory.
117   * @param builder
118   */
119  public FormatterFactory(Builder<?> builder) {
120    this.ssFormat = Objects.requireNonNull(builder.ssFormat, "format can not be null");
121    this.converter = builder.converter;
122    this.containsUserText = builder.containsUserText;
123  }
124
125  /**
126   * The Format used to create factory.
127   * @return format
128   */
129  public SsFormat getSSFormat() {
130    return ssFormat;
131  }
132
133  /**
134   * Convert the string as needed and do
135   * {@link JFormattedTextField#setValue(java.lang.Object) }.
136   * @param ftf set this text field's value
137   * @param string convert to a value
138   * @throws ParseException
139   */
140  public abstract void switchToNonNullValue(JFormattedTextField ftf, String string)
141      throws ParseException;
142
143  /**
144   * Converter used with stringToValue and valueToString; typically null.
145   * @return converter
146   */
147  public AbstractFormatter getConverter() {
148    return converter;
149  }
150
151  /**
152   * Function used to determine if text field has user input; typically null.
153   * @return containsUserText
154   */
155  public BiFunction<JFormattedTextField, AbstractFormatter, Boolean> getContainsUserText() {
156    return containsUserText;
157  }
158
159  /** use setEditValid method to check that formatter should flip */
160  @SuppressWarnings("serial")
161  protected static class NullFormatter extends DefaultFormatter {
162    /**
163     * The null formatter.
164     */
165    public NullFormatter() {
166      // DO NOT CHANGE
167      setValueClass(String.class);
168      // DO NOT CHANGE
169      setCommitsOnValidEdit(true);
170    }
171
172    /**
173     * This method is invoked by the formatter when it is almost done.
174     * After super.setEditValid, if the text field is a String
175     * attempt to set the value (which switches the formatter).
176     * @param valid
177     */
178    @Override
179    protected void setEditValid(boolean valid) {
180      super.setEditValid(valid);
181
182      // if a character was added to the Null Formatter,
183      // then set a value to flip to the  (presumably) edit formatter.
184      final JFormattedTextField ftf = getFormattedTextField();
185      Object value = ftf.getValue();
186      // May not need to check for NullFormatter, but things change :-)
187      if (value instanceof String stringValue && ftf.getFormatter() instanceof NullFormatter
188          && ftf.getFormatterFactory() instanceof FormatterFactory ff) {
189        try {
190          ff.switchToNonNullValue(ftf, stringValue);
191          // If ftf is still the null formatter,
192          // then Formatter didn't like the value; notify and get out.
193          if (ftf.getFormatter() instanceof NullFormatter) {
194            invalidEdit();
195            return;
196          }
197
198          // Attempt to put the caret after the character.
199          try {
200            ftf.setCaretPosition(((String) value).length());
201          } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
202          }
203        } catch (ParseException ex) {
204          // mask formatter (probably) got an exception,
205          // back to the null formatter
206          ftf.setValue(null);
207        }
208      }
209    }
210  }
211}
